purpose: Publish v90 with the bounded pgphoto startup-readiness fix identified from direct K-1 II Polaris logs, while preserving the v89 libgphoto2 and K-3 III control stack.

changes.summary: Extend restart_gphoto readiness from the measured 20-second false-failure window to a bounded 90-second wait for the actual 8080 listener, with an explicit environment override for deterministic tests and future measured tuning.
Add deterministic coverage proving that slow pgphoto readiness succeeds while a hung startup still fails closed, and run the existing deterministic regression suite.
Record the direct v89 K-1 II startup evidence, the readiness-window root cause, the exact fix, and the remaining hardware qualification gates.

known_limits: No libgphoto2 source change is included in v90; the libgphoto2 input remains 63a894b0821a510fc40244c5cc4ef84a5220a91c.
The K-1 II hardware acceptance run must verify one startup without restart churn, normal value-setting latency, preview, ordinary capture, and restoration against the installed v90 identity.
K-3 III ordinary-control regression remains required after installation; timed-B/cancellation remains unqualified under #251 and is not claimed fixed by v90.
A successful offline gate, publication, or install identity check does not by itself prove camera behaviour.
validation_focus: Verify the v90 package records the exact libgphoto2 and patcher commits, stock input hash, ZIP hashes, install manifest, and generated release-change manifest.
Run the canonical pre-release gate and retain its complete transcript with all prerequisite skips explicit.
Deploy through polaris-preflight.sh --wake and release-fwpkt.sh, then verify the device reports 6.0.0.54.90 and the exact on-device provenance.
On K-1 II, compare startup and setting-write latency with v89 and confirm no pgphoto readiness retry occurs while the camera initialises.
On K-3 III, verify startup, populated controls, preview, and ordinary M capture before any separate controlled Bulb qualification.
